intended_object: The tube domain over a base set Ω ⊆ ℝ^n: T_Ω = Ω + iℝ^n = {z ∈ ℂ^n : Re z ∈ Ω}, i.e. the real parts of the coordinates lie in Ω and the imaginary parts are free. This comes from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The body is exactly the textbook definition of a tube domain: it is the set of z : ι → ℂ whose coordinatewise real part, fun i => (z i).re, lies in Ω. Nothing is required of the imaginary parts. This matches T_Ω = Ω + iℝ^n. Degenerate cases also agree: Ω = ∅ gives ∅, and Ω = univ gives univ.

The index type ι is arbitrary, which is at least as general as the usual ℂ^n. One could phrase the notion for the complexification of an abstract real vector space, but the standard notion in several complex variables is stated in coordinates on ℂ^n, so this is not too narrow.

I searched Mathlib for "tube" and found only tube lemmas in topology, with no tube-domain definition. There is therefore no Mathlib counterpart.
